1–2 · READING

Online friends

Before reading: What can go wrong when people treat online contacts like close real-life friends?
Everyone enjoys meeting new people and making friends – and the internet’s made 1 this much easier. However, online friends don’t always behave in the way we expect our real-life friends to. For instance, I recently read about a teenage girl who posted inappropriate photos of a school friend on the web. The photos soon went viral. Over 100 people shared 2 them almost immediately – and 3 thousands more saw and commented on them. Following a complaint from 4 her friend’s parents, the head teacher spoke to the girl. ‘How did 5 this happen?’ 6 he asked. The girl then explained she had more than a thousand online friends, so things spread very quickly. When asked how many of 7 these people were real friends, 8 the girl immediately replied ‘Six!’.

Discuss

What exactly did the girl do wrong?
Why do you think she did it?
Does this story remind you of any similar stories?
How do you keep in touch with close friends and family?
Do you have online friends you have never met in real life?

What do the numbered words refer to?

8 the girl refers to…
3 + 5 · SELF-ASSESSMENT

What kind of an online friend are you?

There is no “correct” personality answer here. Choose the option that is genuinely closest to what you would do, then explain three of your choices aloud.

1. A friend posts and tags a picture of you online without your permission. Do you…
2. A friend often posts pictures of cute animals doing funny things. Do you…
3. A few friends post lots of selfies. Do you…
4. A friend often posts vague status updates like ‘So angry right now!’ Do you…
5. Your brother posts photos of almost every meal he eats. Do you…
6. Your sister often takes online quizzes and wants you to do the same. Do you…
7. A cousin posts inspiring quotes like ‘Follow your dreams.’ Do you…
8. Your grandmother loves online games and wants you to join her. Do you…
9. A friend of a friend sends a friend request and says they like your photo. Do you…
10. An old friend starts posting a lot about his ex-girlfriend. Do you…
After the quiz: Which three choices say the most about you? Which answer would annoy you most if a friend chose it?
4 · VOCABULARY

Online behaviour

tagpermissionmake fun ofunfriendvagueblock
1. If you ______ an online picture, you add the names of the people in it.
2. If someone does something without your ______, they do it before you say it’s OK.
3. If you ______ fun of someone, you laugh at them and make jokes about them.
4. If you ______ someone, you remove them from your list of online friends.
5. If you post ______ status updates, it’s not clear how you feel or what has happened.
6. If you ______ someone, you stop them from seeing your status updates, photos, etc.
6–8 · UNDERSTANDING VOCABULARY

Words with the same verb and noun forms

Many English words can work as both a verb and a noun: email, post, comment, quote, stream, update. Two words in the set behave differently: accept → acceptance and ignore → ignorance.
1. She ______ all these awful photos of her ex-boyfriend online last week.
2. I wanted to ______ on that post, but I just didn’t have time.
3. I know. I saw her status ______ on Facebook earlier.
4. Can you ______ me the details later?
5. To ______ my dad: your best friends are made by time.
6. We managed to find a live ______ and so we watched the game online.
